intro.name: The feast
intro.text:
The village has invited a group of Isolan neighbors to a shared feast. Everyone is supposed to bring a favorite dish and a story about it.
Unfortunately, the villagers disagree about {A}.
(Organizer), the village organizer, wants to {B.1}. The visiting Isolan organizer prefers {B.2}.

text_only.reason: narrative: the occasion; the food reward is on the ending page

choices.label: Let the guests choose the order.

two.text: The hosts make room for both traditions without demanding that either group abandon its own practice.

t1.text: The meal proceeds peacefully, and several villagers learn something new about their neighbors.

t2.text: The arrangements are confusing at first, but a few friendly explanations solve the problem.

t3.text: Everyone is so determined to be polite that nobody starts eating until a child asks whether the food is supposed to get cold.

new.text: The organizers combine elements of both celebrations.

text_only.reason: narrative: the two feasts' customs, not the Celebrating action

n1.text: The guests are delighted by the result.

n2.text: The new ceremony is lovely but takes an absurdly long time.

n3.text: One elder dislikes the changes. The organizers listen, then agree to keep the older tradition available too.

text_only.reason: an unnamed elder's opinion, not a game preference

n4.text: A child invents a ridiculous ceremonial dance. By the end, half the village is doing it.

guests.text: The hosts ask their visitors what would make them comfortable.

g1.text: The visitors appreciate the gesture and suggest an easy compromise.

g2.text: The Isolan organizer admits (isolan.he/she) was hoping the hosts would decide. Both organizers burst out laughing.

g3.text: The visitors choose a custom that the village already follows. Everyone wonders what the argument was about.

taste.text: Both communities present their favorite dishes. A neutral visitor agrees to judge them.

d1.text: The village wins for flavor, while the Isolans win for presentation.

d2.text: The Isolans win by a hair. The village cook asks for the recipe.

d3.text: The judge declares a tie and requests another helping of both.

d4.text: The judge accidentally tastes a decoration instead of the food. The contest is paused while everyone confirms what is edible.

d5.text: The judge announces that the best dish is a combination of both communities' recipes. The cooks are horrified.
